experimentalUse.fit: fit U/u from a weak-drive subset, then predict all 24 downward 0-to-1 transition shifts without mode-specific coefficients
experimentalUse.heldOut: reserve at least half the modes and two independently calibrated tunable U/u settings; compare the measured weak-drive transitions and leading square-root-in-U/u shifts to the frozen arrays
experimentalUse.failure: mode-specific refits, upward leading shifts, or coefficient patterns inconsistent with the measured G reject the diagonal-cosine joined Hamiltonian
experimentalUse.handoff: use the first systematic failure of the quartic law to set the cutoff and coupling range for exact sparse many-body diagonalization

established: the measured Gram-first eigenvectors fix a 24-component leading anharmonic spectroscopy fingerprint rather than only a linear frequency band
boundary: This is first-order quartic perturbation theory for the 0-to-1 transitions in the semiclassical regime sqrt(U/u)<<1. It omits sixth and higher cosine terms, second-order virtual transitions, compact tunnelling between wells, dissipation, drive-induced mixing and the thermodynamic coupled-wire limit. It is not the exact nonlinear gap.
epistemicStatus: analytic perturbative prediction with executable matrix reconstruction; exact nonlinear spectrum and laboratory realization remain open
